findings.issue_text: getBaseConditions() in packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts:68 returns an unparenthesized top-level expression with mixed AND/OR, so callers composing `WHERE ${baseConditions} AND <extra>` will have the extra predicate bind only to the last OR branch due to precedence, silently loosening the authorization check; the returned fragment should be wrapped in parentheses

`"teamId" = ANY(${teamIds})` at packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts:164 is emitted unconditionally; if teamIds is empty, Prisma sends an empty untyped array and Postgres fails with a type-resolution error, unlike the previous `{ in: [] }` which matched nothing; the empty case should be guarded or the array cast to int[]

InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions at packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts:29 widens the constructor to accept scope 'team' without teamId (and teamId on non-team scopes); previously a type error, such input now fails safeParse silently, sets options to null, and returns `1=0`, yielding an empty result with no signal to the caller that the request was malformed

The 'Caching' describe block was deleted from packages/lib/server/service/__tests__/insightsBooking.integration-test.ts:478, so cachedAuthConditions/cachedFilterConditions (including the null filter-cache sentinel path) have no coverage; a regression to undefined checks would re-run membership/team queries on every call unnoticed

In packages/lib/server/service/__tests__/insightsBooking.integration-test.ts:480 only the 'combine' test executes the generated SQL against the database; org/team/filter-only cases assert only on Prisma.sql object equality, so SQL that is structurally expected but invalid or semantically wrong at runtime (e.g. empty ANY, precedence when combined) is never exercised

goldens.comment: In getBaseConditions(), the else if (filterConditions) and final else branches are unreachable. This is because getAuthorizationConditions() always returns a non-null Prisma.Sql object, making authConditions always truthy, which means only the first two if/else if conditions are ever evaluated.

Fetching userIdsFromOrg only when teamsFromOrg.length > 0 can exclude org-level members for orgs without child teams; consider deriving from teamIds (which includes orgId) or removing the guard so org-only orgs still include member user bookings.

adjudication_records.issue_text: getBaseConditions() in packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts:68 returns an unparenthesized top-level expression with mixed AND/OR, so callers composing `WHERE ${baseConditions} AND <extra>` will have the extra predicate bind only to the last OR branch due to precedence, silently loosening the authorization check; the returned fragment should be wrapped in parentheses

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In the diff, `getBaseConditions()` can return `authConditions` (or `filterConditions`) directly when the other is null. For org/team scopes, `buildOrgAuthorizationCondition()` / `buildTeamAuthorizationCondition()` build an `OR` chain via `reduce` that yields SQL like `((c1) OR (c2)) OR (c3)` **without an outer set of parentheses**. If a caller later composes it as `WHERE ${baseConditions} AND <extra>`, SQL precedence makes it `((c1) OR (c2)) OR ((c3) AND <extra>)`, which weakens the intended constraint. This is a concrete property of the returned SQL fragment in the diff (even though the current test uses `WHERE ${baseConditions}` alone). Wrapping the entire returned fragment in parentheses would prevent this.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `"teamId" = ANY(${teamIds})` at packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts:164 is emitted unconditionally; if teamIds is empty, Prisma sends an empty untyped array and Postgres fails with a type-resolution error, unlike the previous `{ in: [] }` which matched nothing; the empty case should be guarded or the array cast to int[]

adjudication.rationale: In buildOrgAuthorizationCondition(), the SQL fragment is always created as Prisma.sql`("teamId" = ANY(${teamIds})) AND ("isTeamBooking" = true)`, where teamIds comes from teamsFromOrg.map(...). If the org has no child teams, teamIds will be an empty JS array. With raw SQL `= ANY($1)`, an empty parameter array commonly becomes an untyped/unknown array in Postgres, which can trigger “could not determine data type of parameter” unless explicitly cast (e.g., ::int4[]) or the empty case is avoided. The previous Prisma where `{ in: [] }` was safe and simply matched nothing, so this diff plausibly introduces a runtime failure for empty org-team sets.

adjudication_records.issue_text: InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions at packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts:29 widens the constructor to accept scope 'team' without teamId (and teamId on non-team scopes); previously a type error, such input now fails safeParse silently, sets options to null, and returns `1=0`, yielding an empty result with no signal to the caller that the request was malformed

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the constructor parameter type from the validated `InsightsBookingServiceOptions` (the Zod discriminated union) to `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions`, where `scope` can be "team" while `teamId` is optional. Since `this.options` is still stored as `InsightsBookingServiceOptions | null` and the implementation continues to rely on `insightsBookingServiceOptionsSchema.safeParse(options)` (implied by the unchanged `this.options` type and existing pattern), an input like `{ scope: "team", userId, orgId }` can now compile but will fail validation at runtime, resulting in `this.options` being `null`. `buildAuthorizationConditions()` explicitly returns `NOTHING_CONDITION` (`Prisma.sql\`1=0\``) when `!this.options`, so the service yields an empty result with no explicit error/feedback. This is a verifiable behavioral regression from compile-time enforcement to silent runtime denial.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The 'Caching' describe block was deleted from packages/lib/server/service/__tests__/insightsBooking.integration-test.ts:478, so cachedAuthConditions/cachedFilterConditions (including the null filter-cache sentinel path) have no coverage; a regression to undefined checks would re-run membership/team queries on every call unnoticed

adjudication.rationale: The diff does delete the entire "Caching" test describe block, so there is indeed less test coverage for the caching behavior of cachedAuthConditions/cachedFilterConditions and the undefined-vs-null sentinel path. However, this is not a verifiable defect/bug introduced in the code itself: the caching logic still exists and nothing in the diff shows it regressing. The proposed finding’s impact (“a regression … would re-run queries … unnoticed”) is speculative about future changes rather than a concrete problem present in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In packages/lib/server/service/__tests__/insightsBooking.integration-test.ts:480 only the 'combine' test executes the generated SQL against the database; org/team/filter-only cases assert only on Prisma.sql object equality, so SQL that is structurally expected but invalid or semantically wrong at runtime (e.g. empty ANY, precedence when combined) is never exercised

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In the diff, most integration tests were changed from asserting Prisma `where` objects to asserting `Prisma.sql` fragments via `expect(...).toEqual(Prisma.sql`...`)` (e.g., org/team/user scopes and filter conditions). Only the new `getBaseConditions` test actually executes the generated SQL against the database using `$queryRaw` and `WHERE ${baseConditions}`. As a result, invalid SQL or runtime-semantic issues (e.g., operator precedence when combined, empty/odd `ANY(...)` edge cases) in those other generated conditions would not be caught by the suite—only structural equality of the `Prisma.Sql` object is checked. This is a concrete reduction in test verification introduced by the diff.
